title: 2024 HMMT February Guts Problem 6
statement: In triangle \(A B C\), points \(M\) and \(N\) are the midpoints of \(A B\) and \(A C\), respectively, and points \(P\) and \(Q\) trisect \(B C\). Given that \(A, M, N, P\), and \(Q\) lie on a circle and \(B C=1\), compute the area of triangle \(A B C\).

solutions.text:
Note that \(M P \| A Q\), so \(A M P Q\) is an isosceles trapezoid. In particular, we have \(A M=\) \(M B=B P=P Q=\frac{1}{3}\), so \(A B=\frac{2}{3}\). Thus \(A B C\) is isoceles with base 1 and legs \(\frac{2}{3}\), and the height from \(A\) to \(B C\) is \(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{6}\), so the area is \(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{12}\).
